key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not translate into reliable downstream cancer care, with model failure patterns shifting across care phases.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating medical AI across the full care pathway may reveal decision errors and omissions that isolated diagnostic tests miss.
method: Built NPC-RubricBench from longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records across six care phases.
Scored 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs using patient-specific criteria restricted to decision-time evidence.
Compared performance across care phases and broad versus checklist-like prompts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients from two cancer centers, 941 patient-phase units, and 17,688 atomic criteria across five evaluation dimensions.
watch_item: Findings are limited to the evaluated models and disease context; checklist-like prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
